text:
Eve: Quick sync: post-RFC action item - unify cutover interfaces across Dedicated and Private deployments. Right now we have two slightly different operator flows.
Kai: Yea the Dedicated flow uses `redwoodctl cutover --type dedicated` and Private uses `private-cutover.sh`. painful to maintain.
Marcos: Can we design a thin adapter layer: a single `cutover-api` that both flows call, with a pluggable backend that knows how to talk to backing control planes?
Eve: That sounds right. We need to expose consistent status codes and `phase` semantics for tooling.
InfraBot: :wrench: I can implement a shim that exposes `/v1/cutover` with phases: PREPARE, SOFT_REDIRECT, DRAIN, SWAP, VERIFY, ROLLBACK.
Kai: Important that the API returns `expected_state` and `residency_verdict` so UI and operators can make decisions.
Marcos: For Private, we must not call external deploy-bot. adapter should support `run_local` mode where it shells out to on-prem ops scripts but still reports status back.
Eve: Also add a `dry-run` param that simulates steps but never touches route tables or KV leases.
Kai: Telemetry: every phase should emit `cutover.phase_start` and `cutover.phase_end` with latency + error fields. makes dashboards easy.
InfraBot: Will include audit_event webhook and support `--audit=true`. also integrate with existing RBAC tokens.
Marcos: We'll need to version the API from day one `v1alpha1` so we can iterate on semantics without breaking Dedicated customers.
Eve: UX for operators: a single `tools/cutover` CLI that posts JSON to the API and streams events. that avoids copy-paste scripts.
Kai: Edge case: if a tenant has multi-region residency constraints (EU write-only plus global read), the API should take `residency_constraints` array and evaluate at PREPARE time.
Marcos: We'll add `residency_constraints` and `consent_required` flags to the request schema. API returns a resumable `cutover_id`.
Eve: Good. Let's document the error handling: 409 if cutover already in progress, 422 if pre-check failed, 500 for infra.
InfraBot: I'll draft an OpenAPI spec and a minimal go server. prototype in infra/cutover-api repo.
Marcos: I'll work on the Private adapter and test harness. Kai will wire metrics and events.
Eve: Timeline: prototype in 2 weeks, staging integration tests after that. thanks.
Kai: I'll add acceptance tests covering rollback, dry-run, and multi-constraint tenants.
Eve: Tag me on the PRs.
Marcos: Also add a note: adapters should not leak credentials -- run under adapter-managed service accounts.
InfraBot: noted. will include credential handling guidelines in the repo README.
Eve: Great. moving this to action items.
thread_text_short: Plan to build a single cutover API with pluggable adapters for Dedicated and Private, phase semantics, telemetry, and dry-run support.
